Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid

  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

def comps_of(g):
    H,W=len(g),len(g[0]); seen=[[False]*W for _ in range(H)]; out=[]
    for i in range(H):
        for j in range(W):
            if g[i][j] and not seen[i][j]:
                st=[(i,j)]; seen[i][j]=True; c=[]
                while st:
                    y,x=st.pop(); c.append((y,x))
                    for dy,dx in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                        a,b=y+dy,x+dx
                        if 0<=a<H and 0<=b<W and not seen[a][b] and g[a][b]==g[i][j]:
                            seen[a][b]=True; st.append((a,b))
                out.append((g[i][j],sorted(c)))
    return out

def settle(g, up=True):
    H,W=len(g),len(g[0])
    objs=comps_of(g)
    ground_row = 0 if all(x==2 for x in g[0]) else H-1
    objs=[o for o in objs if o[0]!=2]
    objs.sort(key=lambda o: -max(p[0] for p in o[1]))  # bottom-most first
    placed={}
    res=[[0]*W for _ in range(H)]
    for col,pos in objs:
        # try to drop down/up until blocked
        cur=pos[:]
        def blocked(cells):
            if any(r<0 or c<0 or r>=H or c>=W for r,c in cells): return True
            for r,c in cells:
                base=r if up else H-1-r
                nbase=(r-1 if up else r+1)
                nb=(c if up else c)
                if base==nbase: continue
                # cell below target in current placement
                tr,tc=nbase,nb
                occ=res.get(tr,{}).get(tc,0)
                if occ: return True
                # also check target not occupied
                if res[tr][tc]: return True
        step=1 if up else -1
        while True:
            nc=[(r+step,c) for r,c in cur]
            if blocked(nc): break
            cur=nc
        for r,c in cur:
            res[r][c]=col
    return res

def settle(g, up=True):
    H,W=len(g),len(g[0])
    ground = 0 if all(x==2 for x in g[0]) else H-1
    objs=comps_of(g)
    objs=[o for o in objs if o[0]!=2]
    objs.sort(key=lambda o: -max(p[0] for p in o[1]))  # bottom-most first
    res=[[0]*W for _ in range(H)]
    def collides(cells):
        for r,c in cells:
            tr = r-1 if up else r+1
            if not (0<=tr<H and 0<=c<W) or res[tr][c]: return True
        return False
    for col,pos in objs:
        cur=pos[:]
        while True:
            nc=[(r-(1 if up else -1),c) for r,c in cur]
            if collides(nc): break
            cur=nc
        for r,c in cur: res[r][c]=col
    return res

def comps_of(g):
    H,W=len(g),len(g[0]); seen=[[False]*W for _ in range(H)]; out=[]
    for i in range(H):
        for j in range(W):
            if g[i][j] and not seen[i][j]:
                st=[(i,j)]; seen[i][j]=True; c=[]
                while st:
                    y,x=st.pop(); c.append((y,x))
                    for dy,dx in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                        a,b=y+dy,x+dx
                        if 0<=a<H and 0<=b<W and not seen[a][b] and g[a][b]==g[i][j]:
                            seen[a][b]=True; st.append((a,b))
                out.append((g[i][j],sorted(c)))
    return out

def solve(g):
    H,W=len(g),len(g[0])
    ground_row = 0 if all(x==2 for x in g[0]) else H-1
    objs=comps_of(g)
    objs=[o for o in objs if o[0]!=2]
    # 2-line: rebuild as full row at ground_row? in demo 2s stayed only in row9; treat as obstacle anyway
    res=[[0]*W for _ in range(H)]
    res[ground_row]=[2]*W
    objs.sort(key=lambda o:-max(p[0] for p in o[1]))  # bottom-most first
    for col,pos in objs:
        cur=pos[:]
        step=-1 if ground_row==0 else 1
        while True:
            nc=[(r+step,c) for r,c in cur]
            ok=True
            for r,c in nc:
                tr=r+step
                if not (0<=tr<H and 0<=c<W) or res[tr][c]: ok=False;break
            if not ok: break
            cur=nc
        for r,c in cur: res[r][c]=col
    return res

        # distance of each value cell to bar

        # order by proximity to bar: nearest first (these end up adjacent to bar)
        pairs=sorted(zip(dists,vals))

def f(g):
    h=len(g); w=len(g[0])
    out=[row[:] for row in g]
    for r in range(h):
        segs=[]
        c=0
        while c<w:
            if g[r][c]==0: c+=1; continue
            col=g[r][c]; c0=c
            while c<w and g[r][c]==col: c+=1
            segs.append((c0,c-1,col))
        if not segs: continue
        # right-align, later segments get rightmost space
        rem=w-1-segs[-1][-1]  # gap to wall
        # place from right: each segment keeps length
        cur=w-rem
        for s in reversed(segs):
            l,r_,_=s[0],s[1]
            newl=max(0,cur-(s[1]-s[0]+1))
            for k in range(s[1]-s[0]+1):
                out[r][newl+k]=s[2]
